:::caution[Superseded — there are no Mug wakes left; the wake-path map still holds]
Since 2026-08-09 the Mug/Kettle/Cup tier is RETIRED (owner-directed) and held off
by `papercusp-mug-kettle-system`, whose default-OFF **is the delivered end state**.
`pot/watchdog.ts` no longer arms a Mug wake, so the fresh-vs-resume question this
page settles no longer has a Mug to settle it for.

**Still true and still worth reading:** the MAP — which wake paths spawn a fresh
`--session-id` session versus which go through the generic wake-executor
`--resume` delivery channel, and where that decision is actually made
(`harness/spawn.ts`, `orchestrator/src/invoke.ts`,
`events/await/wake-executor.ts`). That plumbing is shared and still carries su
wakes today; only the Mug-specific conclusion is dead.

⚠ Note the su engine loop reads `resolvePotHomeSlug` from `pot/wake` — the pot
substrate is deliberately NOT gated by the retirement (it is what the replacement
system runs on), so do not read "the Mug is retired" as "`pot/*` is dead code".

Canonical account: [The Mug · Kettle · Cup tier is RETIRED](/internal/docs/agent-insights/mug-kettle-cup-tier-is-retired).
:::

## What

A common (and load-bearing) misread: "the Pot Mug RESUMES her prior session
every wake (`claude --resume`), so she's a forever-session with an unbounded
growing transcript." **This is wrong.** Verify before designing on it.

(This page is scoped to the **Mug/hive-operator wake path** specifically — the
**Overwatch/Kettle** role, a sibling live-launch tracked the same way in
`adv_sessions`, is NOT part of this cutover: an ended Overwatch session still
resumes via the generic Channel-2 `--resume` path in `wake-executor.ts`, same
as a bee. `hiveInstallSlugFromLabel()` only matches a `hive · ` label prefix,
never `overwatch · `.)

The Mug's **declared, event, watchdog, and manual wakes are ALL already
fresh-per-wake** — each spawns a brand-new claude session with a fresh session
id and **no carried transcript**. Historically the only path that `--resume`d
the Mug was the *generic* wake-executor inbox/await delivery channel (a
`coord:send` with `wake:true` to her owner id, or an `events:await` she
registered — which her persona tells her not to use) — **that exception is now
closed** (mug-brief-cache-assembly B-01/P-012, see Consequence below):
`wake-executor.ts` detects a hive-operator session (by its `hive · ` labeled
`adv_sessions` row) and routes even that path through the same fresh pot
launch.

## The wake paths (ALL fresh — the last exception closed by P-012)

| Path | Trigger | Mechanism | Session |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time wake | `pot:declare-wake {inSeconds}` | `pot-wake` routine → DBOS routinesTick → `system:blueprint-run` → `fireLaunchBlueprint('pot')` → `POST /harness/:slug/invoke?bpkind=pot` | **FRESH** |
| Event wake | `pot:declare-wake {events}` | reaction rule → `pot:wake` tool → `fireLaunchBlueprint('pot')` → same invoke route | **FRESH** |
| Watchdog recovery | turn-end / boot / 30s tick (`hive/watchdog.ts armFallbackHiveWake`) | `declareHiveTimeWake` → same routine | **FRESH** |
| Manual / user | `pot:wake` | `fireLaunchBlueprint('pot')` → same invoke route | **FRESH** |
| Inbox / await | `coord:send {wake:true}` to her owner id, or her own `events:await` | await pump → `wake-executor.ts executeWake` → detects the `hive ·` label (`hiveInstallSlugFromLabel`) → `defaultFireHiveWake` → `fireLaunchBlueprint('pot')` | **FRESH** (closed exception — was `--resume` before P-012 landed) |

### Where "fresh" is decided

`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/harness/spawn.ts` (the
`/invoke?bpkind=pot` route): mints `nativeSessionId = randomUUID()` **fresh on
every fire** and passes it as `PAPERCUSP_NATIVE_SESSION_ID`. Then
`libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/invoke.ts` turns that into
`claude --session-id <uuid>` — which **creates a new session**, never `--resume`.
Because the uuid is freshly minted each fire, no transcript is ever continued.
(For a Codex-backend Mug the CLI accepts no forced session id, but the same
freshly-minted uuid is still recorded as the transcript/roster key — the
`--session-id`/no-transcript-carried argument holds identically for both
backends.)

The session id is *recorded* in `adv_sessions` so the **inbox/await** path
(wake-executor) *could* later `claude --resume <that id>` — but that path
resumes the LAST short fresh session (one turn), never a forever-transcript.

### The easy way to get it wrong

The misread conflates three true-but-unrelated facts: (a) the CUP forced
session id at `operator-spawn.ts:646-656` (that's `cup:spawn`, recorded so a
cup *pane* can `--resume`); (b) the `spawn.ts` comment noting a cup's
`coord:send {wake:true}` resumes the Mug via wake-executor; (c)
`resumeCommandFor` building `claude --resume`. None of those is the Mug's
scheduled-wake path.

## Consequence

- The Mug ALREADY re-derives her working state from durable world-state every
  scheduled wake — and it works. Her load-bearing cross-wake state lives in
  durable artifacts (work-item claims, `blocked_by` edges, priorities, the
  `pot:declare-wake` routine, presence, the decision ledger), not the
  transcript.
- **The cutover has now landed** — the Mug is **uniformly** fresh-per-wake;
  the "one exception" row in the table above is closed. `wake-executor.ts
  executeWake` detects a hive-operator session by its `adv_sessions` label
  (`hive · <slug>/<role>`, `hiveInstallSlugFromLabel()`) and routes its
  ended-session wake through the SAME fresh pot launch (`defaultFireHiveWake`
  → `fireLaunchBlueprint(HIVE_BLUEPRINT_ID, ...)`, the wake text as kickoff)
  instead of `resumeCommandFor` — so an inbox-wake or an `events:await` firing
  on an ended Mug session no longer resumes a stale transcript. A
  wake-floor debounce (`withinWakeFloor`/`effectiveHiveWakeFloorSec`) collapses
  a burst of cup-wakes within the floor window to one fresh launch. On
  fire-failure: PARK, never resume (the always-armed time/watchdog wake
  re-surveys). All other (non-Mug) agents still resume as before.
  (mug-brief-cache-assembly B-01 / P-012, channel `pot-fresh-wake`.)

## How to verify

`grep -n 'randomUUID\|--session-id' spawn.ts invoke.ts` shows the fresh mint +
`--session-id` create. `resumeCommandFor` (`--resume`) is reached only from
`executeWake`, which is the await/inbox pump — not the pot routine/blueprint
path. Don't trust a prose claim that "the Mug resumes" without tracing the
`fireLaunchBlueprint('pot') → invoke?bpkind=pot → --session-id` chain.
